performance_tasks.brief:
(1) Which observation best distinguishes chemical change from a change of state?
A. The shape changes
B. Bubbles appear
C. A new substance forms
D. The sample becomes warmer [1]

(2) Which description explains an endothermic reaction?
A. It absorbs energy from surroundings
B. It releases energy to surroundings
C. It has no energy change
D. It requires no starting energy [1]

(3) What heat is gained by 50 g water warming by 4 °C, with c=4.2 J/(g °C) and q=mcΔT?
A. 840 J
B. 52.5 J
C. 0.84 J
D. 210 J [1]

(4) Why can a burning fuel warm a pan?
A. Breaking fuel bonds is the heat-releasing step
B. The pan heats because fuel absorbs energy
C. Combustion transfers energy to the pan
D. Heat release requires the pan to react [1]

(5) Which comparison of wind generation with fuel combustion is sound?
A. No operating combustion; weather-dependent output
B. Low operating emissions; weather-independent output
C. No fuel combustion; no construction impacts
D. Variable weather dependence; no energy transfer [1]

(6) What does a steeper gradient on a gas-volume against time curve mean?
A. A larger final gas volume
B. A slower gas-production rate
C. A smaller final gas volume
D. A higher gas-production rate [1]

(7) Why can higher solution concentration increase rate at constant temperature?
A. Average particle kinetic energy increases
B. The activation-energy barrier becomes lower
C. Collisions transfer greater energy individually
D. Successful collisions occur more frequently [1]

(8) How does a suitable catalyst increase reaction rate?
A. By increasing the energy of the products
B. By raising the equilibrium concentration of products
C. By offering a lower-activation-energy pathway
D. By increasing the temperature without energy input [1]

(9) What are protein catalysts called?
A. Electrolytes
B. Enzymes
C. Indicators
D. Isotopes [1]

(10) Why can adding water restore blue colour to white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate?
A. Copper metal dissolves without oxidising
B. A different blue oxide forms
C. Sulfate changes to another anion
D. The blue hydrated salt reforms [1]

(11) A(aq) + B(aq) ⇌ C(aq) is at equilibrium. What response follows removal of some C at fixed temperature?
A. No shift; equilibrium remains unchanged
B. Forward shift; more C forms
C. Both forward and reverse reactions stop
D. Reverse shift; more A and B form [1]

(12) Which is the electron-transfer definition of oxidation?
A. Proton gain
B. Electron loss
C. Electron gain
D. Neutron loss [1]
marking_guidance_must_name: Part 1: Correct option C (1). C. A new substance forms. New substance formation defines chemical change. Distractor explanations: A: Shape can change without forming a new substance. B: Boiling can produce bubbles without chemical change. D: Heating alone can raise temperature without chemical change. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 2: Correct option A (1). A. It absorbs energy from surroundings. Energy enters the reacting system. Distractor explanations: B: Releasing energy describes an exothermic reaction. C: Endothermic reactions have an energy change. D: Endothermic does not mean zero activation energy. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 3: Correct option A (1). A. 840 J. 50×4.2×4=840 J. Distractor explanations: B: This results from dividing by the temperature change rather than multiplying. C: 0.84 is the value in kJ, not J. D: This omits the 4 °C temperature increase. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 4: Correct option C (1). C. Combustion transfers energy to the pan. Net reaction energy is transferred to the surroundings. Distractor explanations: A: Breaking bonds requires energy; net release depends on forming product bonds. B: Energy is transferred from combustion to the pan, not absorbed by the fuel from it. D: The pan can warm by heat transfer without reacting chemically. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 5: Correct option A (1). A. No operating combustion; weather-dependent output. Moving air supplies energy without on-site fuel burning. Distractor explanations: B: Wind output depends on wind speed and availability. C: Manufacture and construction still have environmental impacts. D: Wind generation transfers kinetic energy into electrical energy. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 6: Correct option D (1). D. A higher gas-production rate. Gradient is change in volume per unit time. Distractor explanations: A: Gradient measures rate, not the final collected volume. B: A steeper rising curve means a faster, not slower, rate. C: Final volume is read at the plateau, not from steepness. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 7: Correct option D (1). D. Successful collisions occur more frequently. Concentration changes particle number per unit volume. Distractor explanations: A: At constant temperature, average kinetic energy does not increase. B: Concentration does not lower the activation-energy barrier. C: Concentration changes encounter frequency, not the energy of each collision. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 8: Correct option C (1). C. By offering a lower-activation-energy pathway. More collisions can succeed along the lower-barrier pathway. Distractor explanations: A: A catalyst changes the pathway, not product energy levels. B: It does not shift equilibrium composition. D: Catalysis does not create a temperature increase without energy transfer. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 9: Correct option B (1). B. Enzymes. Enzymes are biological protein catalysts. Distractor explanations: A: Electrolytes conduct through mobile ions; this is not the name of protein catalysts. C: Indicators signal conditions such as pH, rather than naming protein catalysts. D: Isotopes are atoms of one element with different neutron counts. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 10: Correct option D (1). D. The blue hydrated salt reforms. Hydration reverses the intended dehydration change. Distractor explanations: A: The starting substance is copper sulfate, not copper metal. B: The product is hydrated sulfate, not a new oxide. C: The sulfate ion remains sulfate; hydration changes water association. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 11: Correct option B (1). B. Forward shift; more C forms. The response tends to replace removed product. Distractor explanations: A: Removing C disturbs equilibrium composition. C: Both reactions continue; neither simply stops. D: A reverse shift would remove more C rather than replace some of it. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 12: Correct option B (1). B. Electron loss. Oxidation is electron loss. Distractor explanations: A: Proton transfer defines acid–base behaviour, not oxidation. C: Electron gain is reduction. D: Neutron loss is a nuclear process, not this redox definition. No mark for more than one selected option.
